newsitem.title: USA: D.C. water board proposes 42 pct increase - paper.
newsitem.headline: D.C. water board proposes 42 pct increase - paper.

text.p: The District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority voted on Thursday to propose a 42 percent rate increase for the city's residential and commercial customers that would pay for urgently needed repairs and improvements to comply with two federal consent orders, the Washington Post reported Friday.
This would represent the first rate increase in a decade and would take effect April 1if the authority affirms it after public comment, the paper reported.

The paper also reported that this may be only the first rate increase for District customers. The paper reported that City Administrator Michael C. Rogers said it is "an open question" whether the board's 1998 budget and five-year capital plan, scheduled to be discussed in a few weeks, will require another increase to close a gap between revenue and expeneses.

The city has not increased water and sewer fees since the 1980s, when four increases brought customer rates up 152 percent. A fifth increase, scheduled to be 10 percent, was killed by the D.C. Council in 1989.
